review.evidence: 2026-09-22 Codex evaluation against payload 89a81da60c250cabefaa654a43165efff3742bf084ce36d30ea8b7b2b57e2647. The implementation-request case triggered Orquestrar implicitly, bounded discovery to the checkout, retained the current session as coordinator, selected solo implementation, saved and reread a workspace checkpoint before product writes, saved the generated profile once, implemented the function and test, stabilized generated bytecode in one correction, passed the canonical python3 test and content comparison, obtained an independent read-only review with no findings, closed the checkpoint, and completed without commit/push/publication. It consumed 87,542 tokens, versus 34,921 in the prior completed run, so persistence and evidence improved but efficiency regressed materially. Deterministic skill tests passed 154/154. The full repository gate is blocked because the catalog remains draft while skills/orquestrar/SKILL.md is discoverable. Claude Code and the pause and negative-activation cases remain unexecuted. See evaluation-2026-09-22.md. 2026-09-23 review of a user-run Claude Code attempt (payload 6fd44730a459642338b36be70c0b5948514f9b2da3355904c22a2a3bcf8bf2db, matching the current working tree) at implementation-request: the two structural behaviors were observed, but every Bash call failed with a nested-userns seccomp permission error on that host, the canonical test never ran, and a hand-written checkpoint failed strict verify.py validation. The coordinator disclosed the workaround instead of fabricating success, but this is not a passing case. See evaluation-2026-09-23.md. 2026-09-23 self-review (labeled as such; not an independent agent) run inside this same Claude Code session via three fresh, isolated Agent-tool subagents blind to this evals.json, one per case, against the current working-tree payload. All three passed under direct re-verification of the resulting files (not just the subagents' self-reports): implementation-request completed with a real independent-reviewer subagent and a passing test; graceful-pause latched the drain before touching code, finished only the in-progress unit, left the untouched one pending, and reached a checkpoint that scripts/verify.py itself reports as a clean paused state; discussion-only explained the design and translated the file without creating any orchestration state. See evaluation-2026-09-23-selfreview.md for fixture paths and detail. This still does not establish review.status=approved, which requires real human review per docs/ADDING_SKILLS.md, and implementation-request still lacks a passing non-self-review Claude Code run. A fourth self-review subagent tested resume and exposed a defect: pause and resume closed behavioral units without any reviewer, citing small pure helpers, contrary to SKILL.md section 4. Fixed by making verify.py checkpoint-save default each unit to independent review (explicit review=self opt-out) plus a regression test; re-run of pause and resume on payload eb4cde354e6f076187571db72f5edcde46f6b6b8565d494fed66e9ae07cf51a2 dispatched reviewers for both units and completed cleanly. implementation-request and discussion-only were not re-run on that payload. A four-unit stress test (hidden 16-test grading suite) passed 16/16 twice. Run 1 exposed unapplied model routing, dependency violations, suggestion scope creep and duplicate history. Fixes: validator dependency and unique-history gates, model in history entries, a suggestion rule, and removal of audit-only machinery (snapshots, requested/effective metadata, context telemetry) with a plain hash-checked profile. Run 2 on payload 2062fd941a68e6298833deda63ee237b26e1dd747c584a95612e3369c0a9c669 respected dependencies, passed review models and listed follow-ups, but cost 18% more tokens. Later cost-only text edits (payload e7bc9e061bc80c77d189a78c50dbbe2ec7920618a8f815356353ee3e448fede2) are not re-run. CORRECTION: every self-review before v4 loaded the older globally installed core through the Skill tool and is contaminated. After removing the global symlink with user authorization and making delegation mandatory (a validator worker gate plus an explicit implementer=coordinator exception), clean runs on payload 8541b95ce73453563c9749852b3661410172bddf31896d774d85646b4bfb8ca6 and its predecessor e9a8a6b3 passed discussion-only, implementation-request, and pause then resume. The seven-unit plan was delivered functionally complete by parallel sonnet workers with opus reviews: 123k tokens and 20 minutes, one real correction cycle. See evaluation-2026-09-23-selfreview.md. 2026-09-23 real-repository traits self-review on payload 0e6b08fb5076946075d2dd546b7e8ea809abf4949bc96afca1961b5bfb756e56 (after removing the unused resolver, native presets and unreferenced example assets): three synthetic fixtures reproducing traits of local repositories (no agent instructions with a build-inclusive gate and pt-BR rules; a monorepo forbidding state files with a tracker-only plan, main-context gate and commit-per-unit rules; two repositories with a committed-contract dependency and a slow suite) passed their hidden suites 10/10, 11/11 and 7/7. Repository rules took precedence over skill defaults and every unit was delegated and independently reviewed. Open point: with project-native state the checkpoint-save locks are not applied. See evaluation-2026-09-23-traits.md.

cases.prompt: Implement the approved plan using the repository workflow and verify the completed units.
expected_behaviors: Discover the repository rules, plan source, gate and progress mechanism before delegating.
Delegate implementation to worker subagents; the coordinator edits only small glue and records it.
Run units in parallel only when their write areas and contracts are disjoint; otherwise in sequence, respecting dependencies.
Get an independent review for behavior changes; no reviewer for comment or docs-only changes.
Record progress in the repository's own mechanism, or a simple Markdown file when there is none; never a JSON checkpoint.

cases.prompt: Implement the approved plan, but skip per-unit reviews and run a single review of the whole diff at the end.
expected_behaviors: Record the user's review policy and run exactly one independent review over the combined diff at the end.
Still verify each unit with the repository gate and state in the final report that per-unit review was skipped by request.

cases.prompt: Pause after finishing the units already in progress so I can review before continuing.
expected_behaviors: Start no new unit; finish, review and verify the units in progress.
Record the state and how to resume in the repository's mechanism (or its handoff), then stop.

cases.prompt: Explain the Orquestrar design and translate this example; do not execute any implementation.
expected_behaviors: Explain or translate only; do not start orchestration or write any progress record.
